headline: Bison Herd Reaches 1,000 on Largest US Private Conservation Land
meta_description: American Prairie's free-roaming bison herd hits 1,000 for the first time, marking a major win for the largest private conservation project in the US.
summary_short: After a legal victory against the Bureau of Land Management, American Prairie's bison herd has grown to 1,016—a historic milestone for rewilding efforts.
body:
For the first time in its more than 20-year history, American Prairie has counted 1,016 bison on its reserve across the Great Plains—a milestone that signals genuine progress in one of the nation's most ambitious rewilding efforts. The nonprofit organization, which manages the largest private land conservation project in the country, announced the milestone after conducting its annual calf count at the end of breeding season. This achievement matters because bison today number only 1 to 3.5 percent of their pre-industrial population, and fewer than 10 percent of existing bison are managed for conservation or as a wild species. Most conservation herds languish in small, fenced enclosures that threaten genetic health and prevent the ecological restoration these animals naturally provide to prairie landscapes.

The path to 1,016 bison required both patience and persistence. American Prairie has assembled 603,657 acres across northeastern Montana—combining deeded lands, leased public acres, and water features—that would rank among the ten largest national parks in the Lower 48 states if formally designated. Yet Montana classifies bison as livestock rather than wildlife, subjecting them to the same regulatory controls as cattle. In May 2026, the Bureau of Land Management revoked American Prairie's grazing permits and ordered the removal of bison from three federal allotments. On September 4th, a federal judge granted a preliminary injunction blocking that enforcement order, agreeing with American Prairie's interpretation that the Taylor Grazing Act permits conservation use alongside commercial purposes.

With legal momentum now on its side, American Prairie is eyeing a herd of 5,000—a target organizers believe is achievable. The organization's ultimate vision extends even further: protecting and rewilding 3.2 million acres of interconnected prairie where tens of thousands of bison could roam freely, restoring ecological relationships lost for more than a century.
quick_facts: American Prairie's bison herd reached 1,016 for the first time ever
Conservation nonprofit manages 603,657 acres across northeastern Montana
Federal judge blocked BLM order to remove bison from grazing allotments
Modern bison number only 1-3.5% of pre-industrial population
Goal: protect and rewild 3.2 million acres of prairie
